how.title: How to resize an image online

steps.title: Add your images
steps.text: Drag photos onto the page, choose them from your device or paste them. You can add as many as you like at once.

steps.title: Choose a size
steps.text: Pick a preset such as Instagram or passport photo, or enter your own width and height in pixels, centimeters, millimeters or inches. You can also set a maximum file size, for example 50 KB.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images. Download each picture on its own or get everything in a single ZIP file.

items.title: Private by design
items.text: Your pictures are processed inside your browser. They are never uploaded to a server, so nobody else can see them.

items.title: Free and unlimited
items.text: No account, no watermark, no daily limit and no waiting. Resize one picture or hundreds.

items.title: Sharp results
items.text: A high-quality resizing filter and modern compressors keep small pictures clear and files small.

items.title: Exact file sizes
items.text: Need a photo under 50 KB for a form? Set the limit and the tool finds the best quality that fits.

items.q: Is it really free?
items.a: Yes. There is no sign-up, no trial and no daily limit. The site is paid for by a few clearly labelled advertisements. Very large pictures can be too much for a phone or an old computer, and you will see a message if that happens.

items.q: Are my images uploaded?
items.a: No. Resizing happens on your own device, inside your browser. Your images are never sent to our servers.

items.q: Which formats are supported?
items.a: You can open JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP files, and AVIF where your browser supports it. You can save as JPG, PNG or WebP.

items.q: Will resizing reduce the quality?
items.a: Making a picture smaller keeps it sharp because the tool uses a high-quality filter. Making it larger cannot add detail that is not there, so enlarged pictures look softer. For JPG and WebP you can choose the quality yourself.

items.q: How do I get an image under a size such as 50 KB?
items.a: Turn on Limit the file size, type the number and press Resize images. The tool lowers the quality and, if needed, the dimensions until the file fits. Choose JPG or WebP for the best results, because PNG cannot be reduced that way.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: Yes. The page works in current versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge on phones, tablets and computers. Very large photos can be limited on older phones.

cm.h1: Resize image in cm, mm or inches
cm.intro: Printing and official forms often ask for a size in centimeters or inches instead of pixels. Enter the size and the DPI, and the tool works out the pixels for you.

steps.title: Add your photo
steps.text: Drag it onto the page or choose it from your device.

steps.title: Enter the size
steps.text: Choose cm, mm or in, then type the width and height. Use 300 DPI for good print quality.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the result.

tips: DPI means dots per inch. At 300 DPI, a picture that is 10 cm wide is about 1,181 pixels wide.
Use 300 DPI for prints and 72 to 96 DPI for screens.
Keep Lock aspect ratio on to avoid stretching. Turn it off and choose Crop to fill if you need an exact shape.
On a website only the pixel size matters. DPI matters when a picture is printed.

items.q: How many pixels is one inch?
items.a: It depends on the DPI. At 300 DPI one inch is 300 pixels. At 96 DPI it is 96 pixels.

items.q: Will it print at exactly this size?
items.a: The tool sets the pixel size that matches your size at the DPI you choose. Print the picture at its actual size, or at that DPI, to get the size you asked for.

items.q: What size is a 4 x 6 inch photo?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 4 x 6 inches is 1,200 x 1,800 pixels.

cm.blurb: Set a picture to an exact size in cm, mm or inches.
details: A picture is made of pixels, and a centimeter or an inch is a physical length. DPI (dots per inch) connects the two: at 300 DPI one inch is 300 pixels, so a photo of 3.5 by 4.5 cm is about 413 by 531 pixels. Printers and many forms use 300 DPI.

Choose cm, mm or inches, enter the size from your form and keep the DPI at 300 unless the instructions say otherwise. The tool calculates the pixels for you and can crop the picture to fill the exact shape.

items.q: What is the standard passport photo size?
items.a: It varies. The United States uses 2 x 2 inches (51 x 51 mm). The United Kingdom, the European Union and Australia use 35 x 45 mm. Canada uses 50 x 70 mm.

items.q: Can I use this for a visa photo?
items.a: Yes, if the visa requirement matches one of the sizes. Many visas use the same size as the passport, but some countries have their own, so always check the official rules.

items.q: How many pixels is a passport photo?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 35 x 45 mm is 413 x 531 pixels and 2 x 2 inches is 600 x 600 pixels.

passport.blurb: Resize photos to common passport and visa sizes.
details: Passport, visa and ID photo rules are set by each country and change from time to time. The sizes on this page are common values and a starting point, not a guarantee that a photo will be accepted.

Besides the size in millimeters or pixels, authorities often specify head height, background color, lighting and file size. This tool resizes and crops your photo; it does not check those rules, so read the official instructions before you submit.

items.a: Use 1080 x 1080 pixels for a square post and 1080 x 1350 pixels for a portrait post.

items.q: What size should a YouTube thumbnail be?

social.blurb: Fit pictures to Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and more.
details: Platforms update their recommended sizes now and then, but the aspect ratios stay almost the same: 1:1 and 4:5 for feed posts, 9:16 for stories and reels, and 16:9 for video thumbnails and covers.
Upload at the recommended pixel size or larger. Platforms recompress every picture, so starting with a clean, sharp image gives the best final result. Choose Crop to fill the box to avoid black bars.

details: Choose JPG for photos and for forms that ask for a JPG, PNG for logos, screenshots and pictures with transparent areas, and WebP when you want the smallest file for a website.

Converting does not add detail. Turning a small JPG into a PNG gives a bigger file with the same picture, and turning a PNG into a JPG fills transparent areas with white. There are dedicated pages for PNG to JPG, JPG to PNG and WebP to JPG.

items.q: Can I compress many images at once?

compress.blurb: Make photos smaller without visible loss.
details: JPG and WebP compress by removing detail the eye hardly notices. Lowering the quality from 100 to 80 often cuts the file by more than half with almost no visible change, while going far below 60 starts to show blocks and smudges.
The biggest saving usually comes from reducing the number of pixels. A photo that is 4000 pixels wide but shown at 1000 pixels wastes most of its data, so resize first and then compress.

The tool does both steps for you: it lowers the JPG quality and, only when needed, reduces the number of pixels.

Signatures and simple scans compress very well because they are mostly white paper. Photos of faces with detailed hair or a patterned background need more data, so for those you may need a 50 KB limit instead.

items.q: How do I reduce a photo to 20 KB?

items.q: Is 20 KB the same as 20,000 bytes?

items.q: Can I use this for a signature?

mb5.intro: Email services, application forms and upload pages often accept files up to 5 MB, and photos from a recent phone or camera can be bigger. Add your image and download a file under 5 MB (5,000,000 bytes) that still looks sharp.
mb5.blurb: Get an image under 5 MB for email and uploads.

steps.title: Add your image
steps.text: Drag it here or choose it from your device. Photos of 8 to 20 MB are fine.

steps.title: Keep the 5 MB limit
steps.text: 5 MB is preselected. The tool counts it as 5,000,000 bytes, so the file passes on systems that count 5,000 KB and on those that count 5,120 KB.

steps.title: Resize and download
steps.text: Press Resize images and download the file. The result shows its exact size.

tips: Photos from recent phones are often 5 to 15 MB. Getting under 5 MB usually only needs a small drop in quality, which you will not see on a screen.
Photos fit best as JPG or WebP. A photo saved as PNG is usually several times larger.
Screenshots and logos are better as PNG: they are small already and keep sharp edges.
To send many photos in one email, add them all at once and download the ZIP file.
mb5.detailsTitle: What 5 MB means for a photo
details: Five megabytes is 5,000 kilobytes. A JPG of that size can hold a photo of 4000 by 3000 pixels with very good detail, depending on the picture, which is more than almost any screen shows.
The tool tries the highest quality that fits and shows you the exact result size before you download. It lowers the pixel size only when the limit cannot be reached by quality alone.

items.q: How do I reduce an image to 5 MB?
items.a: Add the image, keep the 5 MB limit that is preselected and press Resize images. The tool finds the highest quality that fits.

items.q: Is 5 MB the same as 5,120 KB?
items.a: On some systems a megabyte counts as 1,024 kilobytes, on others as 1,000. The tool uses the smaller value (5,000 KB, or 5,000,000 bytes), so the file passes on both.

items.q: Does the picture get smaller in pixels?
items.a: Only if it has to. The tool lowers the quality first and reduces the pixel size only when the limit cannot be reached otherwise.

items.q: Is my picture uploaded?
items.a: No. The picture is processed on your device and never uploaded.

pxToIn.title: Pixels to Inches Converter - Free Calculator (DPI)
pxToIn.description: Convert pixels to inches online free: type pixels, pick the DPI and get the print size in inches. Works for photos, documents and screens. Runs on your device.
pxToIn.intro: Type a size in pixels and see how many inches it prints at your DPI. The calculator also shows common print sizes in pixels and links to the free image resizer.
pxToIn.blurb: Convert pixels to inches at any DPI.

steps.title: Enter the size in pixels
steps.text: Type the width, and the height if you need it. The unit is already set to pixels.

steps.title: Choose the DPI
steps.text: Use 300 for print, 96 for a screen, or the number your printer or form uses. The result changes as you type.

steps.title: Read the size
steps.text: The size appears in inches. Change the unit if you prefer another one.

pxToIn.tipsTitle: Tips for converting pixels to inches
tips: Inches = pixels ÷ DPI. At 300 DPI every 300 pixels make one inch.
A picture of 1200 × 1800 pixels prints at 4 × 6 inches at 300 DPI, and at 12.5 × 18.75 inches at 96 DPI.
The same picture is a different size at a different DPI: more DPI means a smaller and sharper print.
Use the swap button to convert inches to pixels.
pxToIn.detailsTitle: How to convert pixels to inches
details: The formula is inches = pixels ÷ DPI. At 300 DPI, which is the usual choice for printing, 1000 pixels is 3.33 inches. At 96 DPI, the standard of a screen in a browser, the same 1000 pixels is 10.42 inches, and at 72 DPI it is 13.89 inches.
A picture has no real size until it is printed, and the DPI is what links pixels to inches. A full HD picture of 1920 × 1080 pixels is 6.4 × 3.6 inches at 300 DPI and 20 × 11.25 inches at 96 DPI.

items.q: How many inches is 1000 pixels?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 1000 pixels is about 3.33 inches. At 96 DPI it is about 10.42 inches.

items.q: How do I convert pixels to inches?
items.a: Divide the pixels by the DPI. Or type the pixels into the calculator above and it does it for you.

items.q: Which DPI should I use?
items.a: Use 300 for printing, and 72 or 96 for pictures that are only shown on a screen.

items.q: Does the DPI change my picture?
items.a: No. The DPI only decides how big the picture is when it is printed. Resize the picture itself with the image resizer.

Use the swap button to convert millimetres to pixels.
pxToMm.detailsTitle: How to convert pixels to mm
details: The formula is millimetres = pixels ÷ DPI × 25.4, because one inch is 25.4 millimetres. At 300 DPI, 1000 pixels is about 84.67 mm. At 96 DPI the same 1000 pixels is about 264.58 mm.

A picture has no real size until it is printed, and the DPI is what links pixels to millimetres. If a form asks for a size in millimetres and you only know the pixels, 300 DPI is the usual value for photos.

items.q: How many mm is 1000 pixels?
items.a: At 300 DPI, 1000 pixels is about 84.67 mm. At 96 DPI it is about 264.58 mm.

items.q: How do I convert pixels to mm?
items.a: Divide the pixels by the DPI and multiply by 25.4. Or type the pixels into the calculator above and it does it for you.

items.q: Which DPI should I use?
items.a: Use 300 for printing and passport or ID photos, and 72 or 96 for pictures that are only shown on a screen.

items.q: Does the DPI change my picture?
items.a: No. The DPI only decides how big the picture is when it is printed. Resize the picture itself with the image resizer.

paperPx.description: A4 size in pixels at 72, 96, 150, 300 and 600 DPI, plus A3, A5, A6, Letter and Legal in one table, with a free calculator. Runs on your device.

paperPx.intro: How many pixels is an A4 page? It depends on the DPI. The table shows the common paper sizes in pixels at five DPI values, and the calculator converts any other size.

paperPx.tipsTitle: Tips for paper sizes in pixels
tips: A4 at 300 DPI is 2480 × 3508 pixels: the size to use for a sharp print.
For a document that is only shown on a screen, A4 at 96 DPI (794 × 1123 pixels) is enough.
A4 at 72 DPI is 595 × 842 pixels, the size of a PDF page in points.
US Letter is shorter and wider than A4: 2550 × 3300 pixels at 300 DPI.
paperPx.detailsTitle: Why paper has no single pixel size
details: Paper has a real size in millimetres or inches, and a picture has pixels. The DPI (dots per inch) links the two: A4 is 210 × 297 mm, which is 2480 × 3508 pixels at 300 DPI but only 794 × 1123 pixels at 96 DPI.
The ISO A series halves the page each time: A4 is half of A3 and twice A5, and all of them share the same proportions. US Letter, Legal and Tabloid come from inches and have other proportions.

items.q: What is A4 size in pixels?
items.a: At 300 DPI, A4 is 2480 × 3508 pixels. At 150 DPI it is 1240 × 1754, at 96 DPI 794 × 1123 and at 72 DPI 595 × 842.

items.q: What is US Letter size in pixels?
items.a: At 300 DPI, US Letter (8.5 × 11 inches) is 2550 × 3300 pixels. At 96 DPI it is 816 × 1056.

items.q: What is A5 size in pixels?
items.a: At 300 DPI, A5 is 1748 × 2480 pixels. At 96 DPI it is 559 × 794.

items.q: Which DPI should I use?
items.a: Use 300 for printing and 72 or 96 for pictures that are only shown on a screen.

items.q: What is the best size for an Instagram post?
items.a: Use 1080 × 1080 pixels for a square post and 1080 × 1350 pixels for a portrait post, which takes the most space in the feed.

items.q: What size is an Instagram story or reel?
items.a: 1080 × 1920 pixels, which is 9:16, the full height of a phone screen.

items.q: How do I post a whole photo without cropping?
items.a: Choose the Instagram size under Preset, then choose Fit inside the box instead of Crop to fill. The whole picture stays visible and nothing is trimmed.

items.q: What size is an Instagram profile picture?
items.a: Upload at least 320 × 320 pixels. Instagram shows it as a circle, so keep the face in the middle.
